name: Ona Voss
life: Ona repaired hotel menus before anybody entrusted her with books. She earns more rebinding legal registers, but a child's uneven stitches still hold her attention longer than a perfect office volume. People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Ona by a small Wednesday habit. Ona knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I can tell a right-handed child did the sewing. The knots point away from the working hand. I brought thread for visitors to try it before they believe me.
appearance: Ona has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, and a favorite piece of clothing, a rust-colored canvas coat. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Ona gives a little nod before asking a hard question.
personality: Ona finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To teach pupils to read the direction of the stitches.
family: Drew Silva is Ona’s stepsibling. Ona makes the call. Drew is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *First shift back*, Drew says, “I trained under the returning worker. Now we have to admit I'm the one who knows the new forms.”
connections: Rene Mott. They compare the age of the paste with the direction of a child's hand stitches.

reactions.situation: A collector offers cash for the unexamined atlas
reactions.response: Ona asks the bookseller to put the atlas somewhere safe while its ownership is checked.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Ona suggests one straightforward message without accusations and gives the friend time to answer.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Ona waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
